item.title: Fher Olvera from Maná on His Inclusion in Dua Lipa’s ‘Live From Mexico City’ Album: ‘It’s a Source of Pride’
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest music trends. Today, we're talking about a iconic song that's taken on a new life. Maná's "Oye Mi Amor" has been reimagined by none other than Dua Lipa, and it's now part of her new album, Live From Mexico City.
[Short music transition]
Host: The song was recorded during Dua Lipa's Radical Optimism Tour in Mexico City last December, where she invited Maná's vocalist, Fher Olvera, to join her on stage. Olvera shared his thoughts on the collaboration, saying, "Singing 'Oye Mi Amor' with an international artist like Dua Lipa was very special. It's an emblematic song for Maná, and it's been a fundamental song in our career."
[Short music clip from "Oye Mi Amor"]
Host: "Oye Mi Amor" was written by Olvera and drummer Álex González, and it was featured in Maná's 1992 album ¿Dónde Jugarán Los Niños?. The song has become a classic in Latin American music, and its inclusion in Dua Lipa's album is a testament to its enduring popularity.
[Short music transition]
Host: This collaboration is not the only time Dua Lipa has shown her love for Latin American music. During her tour, she performed covers of local artists, including Consuelito Velázquez's "Bésame Mucho" and Selena's "Amor Prohibido". It's clear that Dua Lipa has a special connection with the Latin American audience, and this album is a celebration of that.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for today. Thanks for tuning in to our podcast. If you want to hear more about Dua Lipa's album and her connection to Latin American music, be sure to check out our links in the show notes. Until next time, keep on grooving!
